items.q: On a distance-time graph, what does a flat section mean?
hints: Think about what a zero gradient (no change in distance over time) represents.
If distance isn't changing while time passes, the object isn't moving.

items.q: On a distance-time graph, what does a steeper line mean?
hints: Recall what the gradient of a distance-time graph represents.
A steeper gradient means more distance is covered in the same time.

items.q: A journey covers 120 km in 3 hours on a travel graph. Find the average speed.
A travel graph goes from 0 km to 90 km in 1.5 hours. Find the speed.
A section slopes downwards on a distance-time graph. What does this mean?
hints: Think about what decreasing distance over time represents.
As time passes, the distance from the starting point is getting smaller.

items.q: If a travel graph is horizontal for 20 minutes, what is happening?
hints: Think about what a zero gradient (no change in distance over time) represents.
A horizontal section means the distance stays constant while time passes.

items.q: A journey covers 60 km in 2 hours, then the traveller rests for 1 hour, then covers 40 km in 1 hour. Find the average speed for the whole 4-hour journey (including the rest).
hints: Average speed = total distance / total time — the rest still counts in the total time.
